metadata.methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 25 subjects using 16 electrodes (F7, F3, F4, F8, T7, C3, Cz, C4, T8, P7, P3, Pz, P4, P8, O1, O2) in a standard 10-20 montage at a sampling rate of 128 Hz using NeXus-32 hardware (MindMedia/TMSi) with OpenVibe software. The experiment employed a visual P300 paradigm with repetitive flashing of alien groups (12 groups of 6 aliens, 12 flashes per repetition with 2 targets and 10 non-targets). Participants were instructed to silently count target flashes while minimizing eye blinks and head movements. Data were recorded with a hardware common average reference and ground at FZ, with wet silver/silver chloride electrodes.

citation_details.title: P300 dataset BI2012 from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
citation_details.author: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings from 25 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task inspired by the Space Invaders video game. Participants were presented with visual flashes of alien groups while 16-channel EEG was recorded at 128 Hz, with the objective of detecting target versus non-target stimuli. The dataset includes both training and online sessions with a total of 128 target trials and 640 non-target trials per subject, providing a benchmark resource for P300-based BCI research and algorithm development.

citation_details.title: Van Veen, Barachant & Andreev 2012 — Building Brain Invaders: EEG data of an experimental validation (BI2012)
citation_details.author: G.F.P. Van Veen, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, G. Cattan, P. Rodrigues, M. Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 25 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task based on the Brain Invaders paradigm. Participants viewed flashing alien groups and silently counted target stimuli while 16-channel EEG was recorded at 128 Hz. The dataset includes both training and online sessions with performance feedback, providing a benchmark resource for P300-based BCI research and algorithm validation.

citation_details.title: Vaineau, Barachant & Andreev 2013 — Brain Invaders Adaptive versus Non-Adaptive P300 Brain-Computer Interface dataset (BI2013a)
citation_details.author: E. Vaineau, A. Barachant, A. Andreev, P. Rodrigues, G. Cattan, M. Congedo
citation_details.abstract: This dataset comprises electroencephalographic recordings from 24 healthy subjects performing a visual P300 brain-computer interface task based on the Brain Invaders video game paradigm. The study compares P300-based BCI performance with and without adaptive calibration using Riemannian geometry methods. EEG data were acquired using 16 electrodes across 8 sessions per subject, with each session containing training and online phases in both adaptive and non-adaptive modes. Training phases consisted of 80 target and 400 non-target flashes per phase, while online phases contained variable numbers of trials based on user performance.
